item.title: Hong Kong mulls legislation to tackle AI ‘deepfake’ porn – official
item.description: An inter-departmental working group set up by Hong Kong’s justice department is studying whether to set up legislation for cases involving indecent images generated by Artificial Intelligence (AI), following an AI-porn scandal at a local university. In response to lawmakers’ questions on Wednesday, Acting Secretary for Innovation, Technology and Industry Lillian Cheong said in Cantonese […]

item.title: HK$4.5 billion raised in public fund for Tai Po fire victims, gov’t says
item.description: Around HK$4.5 billion has been raised in the Hong Kong government’s public donation fund for victims of the deadly Tai Po fire. Secretary for Home and Youth Affairs Alice Mak gave the updated figure for the Support Fund for Wang Fuk Court in Tai Po in response to a lawmaker’s question during a Legislative Council […]

item.title: Hong Kong to address comfort, hygiene concerns over seat belt law, as lawmakers urge review
item.description: Authorities will address comfort and hygiene concerns over a new law requiring passengers to wear seat belts on buses, transport chief Mable Chan has said. Addressing the press at the Legislative Council after meeting lawmakers on Wednesday, Chan said she had noted the public’s comments about inconvenience and discomfort regarding the wearing of seat belts […]

item.description: By Tommy Wang Hong Kong residents hoping to cash in on a precious metals rally are buying up bars of silver as an alternative to gold that they say has become “too expensive” after reaching record highs. item.title: ‘Many errors’ in prosecutors’ transcripts of Tiananmen vigil activists’ speeches, Hong Kong national security judge says
item.description: A Hong Kong court has heard recordings of years-old speeches made by two Tiananmen vigil activists facing national security charges, with a judge noting that the transcripts prepared by the prosecution contained “many errors.” Prosecutors on Thursday began playing footage of speeches made by Lee Cheuk-yan and Chow Hang-tung during Tiananmen vigils after concluding their […]

item.title: UK PM Starmer reports ‘good progress’ after meeting China’s Xi; 30-day visa free travel for British tourists
item.description: By Isabel Kua and Marie Heuclin Britain’s Prime Minister Keir Starmer hailed “really good progress” on issues including visa-free travel and tariffs during talks with Chinese leader Xi Jinping in Beijing on Thursday. item.title: Hong Kong gov’t to approve dog-friendly restaurant permits mid-2026
item.description: The Hong Kong government has announced that pet dogs will be allowed in some restaurants as early as mid-2026. Tse Chin-wan, secretary for environment and ecology, told the Legislative Council (LegCo) on Thursday that authorities would approve the first batch of applications allowing pet dogs in restaurants in the middle of the year. item.title: Severely decomposed 11-metre whale carcass to be removed from Sai Kung beauty spot on Friday
item.description: A severely decomposed 11-metre baleen whale carcass which washed up at a Sai Kung beach will reportedly be removed on Friday. Ham Tin villagers reported a bad smell and alerted authorities on Thursday morning. According to TVB, government personnel in protective gear arrived to handle the remains on Thursday. item.title: 16 firefighters, 4 medics, 3 fire trucks, ambulance respond to man unable to take off bus seatbelt
item.description: Hong Kong bus operator Citybus has filed a police report after it found a piece of aluminium foil stuffed inside a seatbelt buckle, which reportedly left a passenger trapped for over 45 minutes. item.title: Panama’s top court annuls Hong Kong-based CK Hutchison’s canal port concession
item.description: Panama’s Supreme Court annulled on Thursday the concession allowing Hong Kong-based CK Hutchison to operate ports at the Panama Canal, a year after US President Donald Trump threatened to seize the crucial passageway claiming China controlled it.
